# AWS System Design Basics

**Source:** https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeSfbOYJrMU/ · **Type:** Reel · **Author:** Arjay McCandless · **Saved:** 2026-10-10

## Summary

A step-by-step overview of how to compose AWS services to build a full-stack serverless web application architecture. It covers request handling, database storage, infrastructure as code, asset delivery, monitoring, authentication, asynchronous background processing, and custom domain routing.

## Transcript and on-screen text

If you take API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB, you can build a simple serverless API. If you add CloudFormation, you can deploy the entire thing using infrastructure as code. If you add S3, you can store files, images, and videos. And if you add CloudFront, you can serve those assets to users around the world. If you add CloudWatch, you can monitor your application and get alerted when something goes wrong. If you add Cognito, you can let users sign up, log in, and authenticate requests to your API. If you add SQS, you can move slow tasks to the background so users don't have to wait for them. If you add Route 53, you can connect everything to your own domain. Congrats, you just built a pretty solid AWS system. Next episode I'll give you a simple stack to do the same thing for free on your own computer. On-screen text: GET /items, 200 OK, template.yaml, photo.jpg, video.mp4, 600+ edge locations, ALARM: errors > 1%, Sign up - Log in, JWT, 202 Accepted, yourapp.com, ubuntu-vm, localhost, $0/mo, Docker, Kong, Node.js, PostgreSQL, MinIO, NGINX, Prometheus, Keycloak, RabbitMQ, Follow for part 2.
